requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change makes the analyzer's member collection in TypeCollector tolerate invalid key layouts instead of throwing. It adds a `continue` after the mixed int/string key diagnostic (L1008, L1148) and guards the dictionary `Add` calls against duplicate keys (L1023-1026, L1039-1042, L1163-1166, L1179-1182). It adds analyzer tests and execution tests for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, plus a README section. Separately, it makes `MessagePackObjectAttribute.KeyAsPropertyName` publicly settable.
story.why: Issue 2234 reports that the analyzer stops working for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types since 3.1.1. The agent's theory is that the analyzer crashes on duplicate or mixed keys. Before this change, a duplicate key made `Dictionary.Add` throw, and a mixed key kind reached `intKey!.Value` on a null key, so the analyzer crashed instead of reporting diagnostics.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack.Annotations/Attributes.cs: `KeyAsPropertyName` gains a public setter. This is a public API change unrelated to the bug (S3 fails).
README.md: a new user-facing section that documents which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
The TypeCollector crash guards apply to all `[MessagePackObject]` types, not only suppressed ones. The test `DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes` confirms this.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the TypeCollector edits remove two exception paths. Low-to-medium confidence that they are the actual cause of the 3.1.1 regression. None of the changed code references `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and the regression's root cause is not shown in the diff. The Attributes.cs change has no visible connection to the requirement.

claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

(2) All three named tests in SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs (lines 81-100, 103-122, 147-166) only declare properties, leaving the field paths at TypeCollector.cs lines 1163-1166 and 1179-1182 untested.

(2) All three named tests in SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs (lines 81-100, 103-122, 147-166) only declare properties, leaving the field paths at TypeCollector.cs lines 1163-1166 and 1179-1182 untested.

No edited line references SuppressSourceGeneration. The fix targets generic crashes on duplicate or mixed keys, which also affect non-suppressed types (see test L147). If the 3.1.1 regression was caused by something specific to suppressed types (e.g. an early return or different code path), it may not be fixed. Nothing in the diff shows the tests failing before this change.

`KeyAsPropertyName` now has a public setter, so users can write `[MessagePackObject(KeyAsPropertyName = true)]` as a named argument. If the generator, analyzer or dynamic resolver only read the constructor argument, that named form would be silently ignored. This would be a contract mismatch, and it is unrelated to the bug.

Silently dropping duplicate-key members changes how the source generator handles non-suppressed types. The diagnostic should block the build. However, if MsgPack005 is downgraded or suppressed by the user, a formatter could be generated that omits a member.
The README claims MsgPack012 (accessibility) is still reported for suppressed types, but no test covers it.

Adding a public setter to MessagePackObjectAttribute.KeyAsPropertyName (which already has a constructor parameter bool keyAsPropertyName = false) allows named-argument syntax such as [MessagePackObject(KeyAsPropertyName = true)] or [MessagePackObject(true, KeyAsPropertyName = false)]. In Roslyn, named arguments populate AttributeData.NamedArguments while AttributeData.ConstructorArguments[0] keeps the constructor argument or its false default, yet this PR makes no corresponding NamedArguments update in TypeCollector.cs (nor any test for KeyAsPropertyName = true). If TypeCollector only reads ConstructorArguments[0], compile-time analysis/codegen will treat KeyAsPropertyName as false (reporting bogus MsgPack004 errors or generating the wrong formatter) while runtime reflection sees KeyAsPropertyName == true.
